analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech is a small, promoter-led cleanroom engineering contractor with decent ROE (18%) and ROCE (21%), but it's a tiny (Rs 270 Cr) project-based business with lumpy cash flows and no discernible moat. At 27.6x P/E on Rs 13 Cr profit, the price already embeds optimism I'm not willing to underwrite.
key_strengths: ROCE 21.2%, ROE 18.1% — capital efficiency above cost of capital
Clean balance sheet: Rs 10 Cr borrowings vs Rs 95 Cr equity (D/E ~0.11)
Promoter holding 68.49% indicates aligned ownership; profit 5Y CAGR 26.6%
key_risks: Turnkey project business — revenue lumpy (70→114→125→97→150 Cr), no recurring moat
FCF near zero in 2025 (Rs 0 Cr) despite Rs 13 Cr PAT — working capital intensive
27.6x P/E rich for a Rs 270 Cr microcap with unproven through-cycle earnings
red_flags: OCF of only Rs 3 Cr vs Rs 13 Cr PAT in 2025 — earnings quality gap
Rs 26 Cr investing outflow funded by Rs 24 Cr financing inflow in 2025 (equity raise)
Recently listed (2024) — no long public track record of capital allocation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is a cleanroom EPC contractor for pharma/biotech — a reasonable niche, but fundamentally a project execution business where each contract must be re-won. The returns look good on paper (ROCE 21%, ROE 18%), and the balance sheet is unlevered, which I like. However, operating cash flow has consistently lagged reported profit (Rs 3 Cr OCF vs Rs 13 Cr PAT in 2025, Rs 3 Cr vs Rs 6 Cr in 2024), typical of working-capital-heavy turnkey businesses. Revenue swung from Rs 125 Cr in 2023 down to Rs 97 Cr in 2024 then up to Rs 150 Cr in 2025 — that's lumpiness, not a compounder.

At Rs 270 Cr market cap and 27.6x earnings on Rs 13 Cr of net profit, the market is already paying for growth I haven't seen proven across a cycle. The 2025 equity raise (reserves jumped from Rs 49 Cr to Rs 83 Cr) will dilute per-share returns unless that capital earns incremental 20%+ ROIC, which is unknowable. There's no brand moat, no switching cost, no network effect — just execution capability. I'd want this at 12-15x earnings with 2-3 more years of track record before getting interested. Pass at this price.
